newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria issues letter bomb warning.
newsitem.headline: Austria issues letter bomb warning.

text.p: Austrian Interior Minister Caspar Einem warned of a possible wave of racist letter bomb attacks on Tuesday after a device targeting his step-mother exploded without causing injury.
"People who are working to integrate foreigners and are involved with humanitarian groups are particularly at risk," Einem told Austrian radio.

A letter bomb incorrectly addressed to Einem's step-mother Lotte Ingrisch, 66, exploded on Monday after it was returned to the purported sender. The package had been mailed to the home Ingrisch left a year ago.

No group has yet claimed responsibility for the attack but the self-styled Bajuwarischen Liberation Army (BLA) has admitted sending more than a score of racially-motivated letter bombs since 1993, injuring 12.
Chief investigator Robert Sturm said he believed the BLA was behind the latest attack.

Einem said his efforts to find the perpetrators would continue and he expressed confidence in a special police unit that was set up to investigate the bomb campaign. Authorities have made little progress in finding the culprits.
"The special commission is working extremely professionally...(And) I will everything in my power to end this horror," Einem said.

Ingrisch, the widow of composer Gottfried von Einem, said she suspected the bomb could be the work of old sympathisers active under the regime of Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler or younger neo-Nazi fanatics.
